old_text: The pitching the first wicket is to be determined by the cast of a piece of money.
new_text: "The Pitch’ng the first Wicket is to be determined by the Toss of a Piece of Money.

old_text: When the first wicket is pitch’d, and the popping-crease cut, which must be exactly three feet ten inches from the wicket, the other wicket is to be pitch’d directly opposite at twenty-two yards distance, and the either popping-crease cut three feet ten inches before it.
new_text: When the first Wicket is pitch'd, and the Popping-Crease cut, which must be exactly Three Feet Ten Inches from the Wicket, the other Wicket is to be pitch’d directly opposite, at Twenty-Two Yards Distance, and the other Popping-Crease cut Three Feet and Ten Inches before it.

old_text: The stumps must be twenty-two inches long, and the bail six inches.
new_text: must be Twenty-Two Inches long, and the Bail Six Inches.

old_text: The ball must weigh between five and six ounces.
new_text: must weigh between Five & Six Ounces.

old_text: When the wickets are both pitch’d, and all the creases cut, the party that wins the toss-up may order which side shall go in first, at his option.
new_text: When the Wickets are both pitch’d, and all the Creases cut, the Party that wins the Toss-up, may order which Side shall go inn first, at his Option.

old_text: The LAWS for the BOWLERS Four balls and over The bowler must deliver the ball, with one foot behind the crease, even with the wicket: and when he has bowled one ball or more, shall bowl to the number four before he changes wickets, and he shall change but once in the same innings.
new_text: The Bowler must deliver the Ball, with one Foot behind the Crease, even with the Wicket; and when he has bowl’d one Ball, or more, shall bowl to the Number of Four before he changes wickets, and he shall change but once in the same Innings.

word_diff.old: LAWS for the BOWLERS Four balls and over The bowler

old_text: He may order the player that is in at his wicket to stand on which side of it he pleases at a reasonable distance.
new_text: He may order the Player that is inn at his Wicket, to stand on which Side of it he pleases, at a reasonable Distance.

old_text: If he delivers the ball with his hinder foot over the bowling-crease, the umpire shall call no ball, though she be struck, or the player is bowled out; which he shall do without being ask’d, and no person shall have the right to ask him.
new_text: If he delivers the Ball, with his hinder Foot over the Bowling-Crease, the Umpire shall call no Ball, tho’ it be struck, or the Player be bowl’d out; which he shall do without being ask’d, and no Person shall have any Right to question him.

old_text: LAWS for the STRIKERS, or those that are in If the wicket is bowl’d down, it’s out.
new_text: If the Wicket is bowl’d down, it’s out.

old_text: If he strikes or treads down, or he falls himself upon the wicket in striking (but not in over-running) it’s out.
new_text: If he strikes, or treads down, or falls himself upon his Wicket in striking (but not in over-running) it’s out.

old_text: A stroke or nip over or under his bat, or upon his hands (but not arms) if the ball be held before she touches ground, though she be hugg’d to the body, it’s out.
new_text: A Stroke, or Nip, over or under his Bat, or upon his Hands (but not Arms) if the Ball be held before it touches the Ground, though it be hugg’d to the Body, it’s out.

old_text: If in striking both his feet are over the popping-crease, and his wicket put down, except his bat is down within, it’s out.
new_text: If in striking, both his Feet are over the PoppingCrease, and his Wicket put down, except his Bat is down within, it’s out.

old_text: If a ball is nipp’d up, and he strikes her again wilfully before she come to the wicket, it’s out.
new_text: If a Ball is nipp’d up, and he strikes it again wilfully, before it came to the Wicket, it’s out.

old_text: If the players have cross’d each other, he that runs for the wicket that is put down, is out; if they are not cross’d, he that returns is out.
new_text: If the Players have cross’d each other, he that runs for the Wicket that is put down, is out: If they are not crossed, he that returns is out.

old_text: If in running a notch, the wicket is struck down by a throw, before his foot, hand, or bat is over the popping-crease, or a stump is hit by the ball, though the bail was down, it’s out.
new_text: If in running a Notch, the Wicket is struck down by a Throw, before his Foot, Hand, or Bat is over the PoppingCrease, or a Stump hit by the Ball, though the Bail was down, it’s out.

old_text: But if the bail is down before, he that catches the ball must strike a stump out of the ground ball in hand, then it’s out.
new_text: But if the Bail is down before, he that catches the Ball must strike a Stump out of the Ground, Ball in Hand, or else it’s not out.

old_text: If the striker touches, or takes up the ball before she is lain quite still, unless ask’d by the bowler or wicket-keeper, it’s out.
new_text: If the Striker touches, or takes up the Ball before it has lain quite still, unless ask’d by the Bowler, or WicketKeeper, it’s out.

old_text: BAT, FOOT, or HAND over the CREASE When the ball has been in hand by one of the keepers or stoppers, and the player has been at home, he may go where he pleases till the next ball is bowled.
new_text: When the Ball has been in Hand by one of the Keepers, or Stoppers, and the Player has been at Home, he may go where he pleases till the next Ball is bowl’d.

old_text: LaWS for the UMPIRES To allow two minutes for each man to come in when one is out, and ten minutes between each hand.
new_text: To allow Two Minutes for each Man to come inn when one is out, and Ten Minutes between each Hand.

old_text: They are sole judges of all outs and ins, of all fair or unfair play, of all frivolous delays, of all hurts, whether real or pretended, and are discretionally to allow what time they think proper before the game goes on again.
new_text: They are sole Judges of all Outs and Inns: of all fair or unfair Play; of all frivolous Delays; of all Hurts, whether real or pretended, and are discretionaliy to allow what Time they think proper before the Game goes on again.

old_text: In case of a real hurt to a striker, they are to allow another to come in, and the person hurt to come in again: but are not to allow a fresh man to play, on either side, on any account.
new_text: In case of a real Hurt to a Striker, they are to allow another to come inn, and the Person hurt to come inn again; but are not to allow a fresh Man to play, on either Side, on any Account.

old_text: They are sole judges of all hindrances, crossing the players in running, and standing unfair to strike, and in cases of hindrance may order a notch to be scored.
